Mission goal

You have got one year to advance from a small shopkeeper to a trader.

Lubeck's strength is fishing and the production of iron goods. Apart from that, wood and tiles are also produced so it should not be a problem to build new buildings. 

You should therefore concentrate in getting beer from Stetin or Gdansk in the first instance. You could also go to Hamburg or Bremen, but these are further away. 

There is sometimes a lack of iron goods and fish in Danzig. Stetin also urgently needs iron goods. 

Make sure that you do not pay too much for these goods. The limits are somewhere between 450 for fish, 450 for iron goods and 50 for beer.
Mission hint

Because the trade with pig iron is important, you should make sure that there is always enough pig iron available in Lubeck; then this raw material cannot be produced here. But it can, for example, be produced in Oslo. This town is also a grateful importer of grain, iron goods and beer.

You should sell as much of these goods as possible in Lubeck, then that is the quickest way of raising your status, and your advancement to trader will then be quicker. 

Incidentally, in this part of the campaign you should build neither ships nor buildings. We will do that in the next part.

You are on the right way! 
But in order to become a trader, you'll have to start looking after the rich citizens of Lubeck as well. They are not really interested in grain and beer; you should try to satisfy their demand by supplying them with meat, wine and cloth. 

You'll get meat from Aalborg and Bergen. Make sure that Aalborg gets enough salt, otherwise they cannot produce any meat there. You can take the salt with you from Lubeck.

You'll get wine from Cologne; the citizens there could well do with some fish and beer. 

You can get cloth from Bisbee. Find out what they need there.

Normally, your reputation in a town will always then grow, when you supply it with goods. However, this is only valid if the goods are also needed. When a product is no longer needed, there will not be much between the purchasing and selling prices You should keep an eye on this.

Incidentally, you can also lose your standing in a town if you buy up a rare product. So never do that in your hometown!

You will have noticed some small product symbols in various towns on the sea chart. These show you which products are most needed. \nAttention: It could take some time before this information reaches you; it is therefore possible that a symbol becomes invalid, before you reach the town.  If you want to use these symbols to your advantage and make additional profit, then concentrate on the towns in the immediate area in and around Lubeck.
Winter is coming! Buy grain and beer and store it in your trading office so that you are in a position to supply your hometown in winter and thereby increase your standing among its citizens. \n

Remember that your rank is awarded by your hometown; you must therefore do everything in your power to become well known in the town. Your current rank is displayed in the overview of your trading office.\nYou have to do more for the citizens of your hometown in order to advance.\n

In this part of the campaign you must advance from a trader to a merchant. You have six months to do so. Alongside trading, you should now build facilities and houses in your hometown.

As you know, Lubeck is strong in fishing and the production of iron goods. Now build a building of each production. You might eventually have to get the building raw materials from other towns. However, just build one of each type of building for the moment; then you need to find customers for your products.

Building production facilities give you two advantages apart from trading: Firstly, your standing increases with every worker you employ. Secondly, the jobs you are offering attract new citizens to the town. This increases the demand and you can sell more goods.

In order for your production facility to quickly reach full capacity, the poor citizens must at least be satisfied. You should continue to ensure a good supply of goods to the town. Apart from that, the workers need living quarters. If the capacity of the previous houses is not enough to accommodate the workers, then you should build a new house.

Remember that your production facilities need raw materials. This should be available in your trading office. 

If you have a trading office administrator, then he can buy the raw materials from the town, if necessary. That however, is not necessary at the moment, and in any case an administrator only cost money.

To find out what raw materials you need in your production facilities; you have to click them when they are completed. You can also get information on the requirement of your facilities in the town in your trading office.

Essentially, in order to become a merchant, you must gain social recognition and build up considerable wealth. Again, concentrate on wine, meat and cloth. Now add skins to your assortment, you will find these in the East.  

Should you by chance come across spices, then take these with you and sell them also in Lubeck; then the rich are very hot on them.

In order to be able to transport the goods that you produce better, you should own one more ship at least. Place an order at the ship builders in Lubeck for a snaikka or a crayer. 

Use the shipyard in Lubeck as much as possible, including repair work, because the more orders they get the better the ships they build will be.
You are on the right way; your social standing is growing all the time.

Your social standing in Lubeck is sufficient now; try to keep it at this level. 

But you cannot afford to neglect the poorer citizens of the town. If you do not look after a particular group of citizens for a while, then your status will fall again. 

Supply the rich in Lubeck as before, but strengthen your efforts to cover the supply requirement of the poor.

You have achieved enough recognition in Lubeck. 

Unfortunately, you are not wealthy enough to advance to the rank of a merchant. Continue to look after the citizens of Lubeck, and try at the same time to build up greater wealth. 

Good luck.

You only need a bit more social recognition and a bit more wealth to advance from merchant to travelling merchant. Besides that, you have to become a member of the guild; the latter gives you a few more reputation points anyway.

Remember, that it is not only cash, which counts as wealth but also production facilities, houses, ships and goods in stock. Monies that you owe to a lender are deducted.

In case accommodation in Lubeck is becoming short, then you should quickly build the relevant houses, then every tenant- in exactly the same way as every worker you employ- will gets you additional points. If you are not quick enough, then a competitor or the town could build the houses and that would then make it more difficult for you fill your own. Because there is also a weekly property tax on the houses, you have to have a high rate of occupancy in order to make a profit. Half-timbered houses must have an occupancy rate of over 70{%%:00} other houses of over 50{%%:00}.

Have you joined the guild in Lubeck yet? You have to become a member of the guild to advance to a long distance merchant or even higher. Incidentally, the wealthier you are the higher the fee for joining. Besides, it decreases in proportion to your social standing, the higher your status the less you pay.\n

You will have to achieve a decisively higher status among all citizens of the town within a year. Because you have to be considerably wealthier, you should invest as much as possible in your hometown, then investing your money increases your wealth and brings recognition.
Double or triple your production in Lubeck and build houses in time, so that the workers and their families can become your tenants. 
Increasing the production also means that you will have to build new ships, to enable you to transport your products.

Here are few more tips on how to achieve respectability. Basically, you should bear in mind that  everything you do for your hometown; will bring you status points. Donate your money to the church or to the bathhouse; this will increase it. Lend it, or build a building and facilities; this also increases it.  It will also increase through: the family, organising festivities, great wealth or placing outriggers at the disposal of the town. 
Your respectability can sink in the same way if, for example, a crime becomes known, if your production facility is demolished or if you demand too high an interest when lending money.
Incidentally, your status can increase by a successful expedition, then all Hanse towns profit from such undertakings. You can undertake such expeditions from time to time and discover new trans-shipment locations.

So that you can make even more profit, you should build trading offices in as many other towns as possible and produce goods in them. Your own production is not always cheaper than goods, which you can sometimes buy at favourable prices. However, your own production at a constant price and constant quantity makes calculation easier. This is ideal, for example, for setting up trades routes to continuously supply your hometown or to exchange your own products between two or more trading offices.
But be careful in your choice of production facilities. Think carefully about the goods that will be needed in towns in the future. Then if you produce more than you can sell, then surplus goods will have to be held in stock. and as a result of that, your profit will drop permanently.  
If you cannot make a profit from your own production, then do not be afraid of closing or demolishing such a facility.

Your wealth and your social status are now enough for the rank of Councillor. Now start looking after the well to dos and the rich in your hometown, so that your social welfare status also becomes sufficient.

Your wealth and social status are now enough for the rank of Councillor. Now start looking after the poor and the well to dos of your hometown, so that your social welfare status also becomes sufficient.

You must gain a much higher status among all citizens of the town within a year, and because you will have to be far richer, you should invest as much as possible in your hometown; then investment increases your wealth and status.
Double or triple your production in Lubeck, and build houses early enough so that the workers and their families can become your tenants. 
Increasing the production also means, that you will have to build new ships in order to transport the products you will produce.
Above all, you must gain popularity in hometown in order to attain the rank of a Patrician. Once you have attained this, then the office of Lord Mayor will be open to you.\n

In order to become Lord Mayor, you have to surpass the current Lord Mayor in popularity. You are also allowed to surpass other influential citizens of the town.  You can find out if, and where you are, on the candidates list by looking under the rubric "town info" in the council office.
If you have made it to Lord Mayor, you can then strive for the office of Alderman. This is awarded at the Hanse conference. You status in other towns counts for this as well; then all the Hanse towns elect the Chairman of the Hanse. Incidentally, a quick visit to the bathhouse could be helpful.

Good luck.
June 5th, 1305 - Pope Clement V is elected
Bertrand de Got, Archbishop of Bordeaux, is elected Pope in the presence of Philip IV, King of France.
1309 - Pope Clement V relocates his residence to Avignon
Under pressure from King Philip IV, Pope Clement V relocates the papal residence to Avignon, very much to the anger of the Royal Houses of England and Germany.
October 20th, 1314 - Electoral Princes appoint Louis IV King
After the victorious battle against Frederic of Austria, Louis IV of Bavaria is appointed King of Germany.
August 7th, 1316 - First papal election in Avignon
John XXII is the first pope elected in Avignon. This is the beginning of a power struggle between the Pope and King Louis IV. of Germany.
October 8th, 1323 - The Pope does not recognize King Louis
Pope John XXII that of Louis IV abdicate, as he was elected without papal approval and has no valid legitimacy as king.
March 1324 - Louis IV is excommunicated by the Pope
King Louis IV, refusing to abdicate, is excommunicated by the Pope.
January 29th, 1327 - Edward III becomes King of England
Edward III is crowned king at the age of 15. The reign of government, though, is taken over by Lord Roger Mortimer, beloved of Edward's mother Isabella of France.
January 11th, 1328 - Ludwig IV receives Imperial crown from the people
Louis IV. has himself elected and crowned Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire by the people of Rome. Custom demands that he receive the crown from the Pope.
November 1330 - Edward III has Mortimer murdered
The young King Edward III captures Regent Mortimer and has him assassinated for finally making himself ruler of England.
Dezember 20th, 1334 - New Pope: Benedict XII
Pope Benedict XII does not recognize Louis the Bavarian, just as he had done before with his predecessor. Building a new papal palace in Avignon, he also shows his intention of not returning to Rome.
August 4th, 1338 - Louis IV provokes Pope Benedict
Louis IV  provokes the Pope once again by declaring that the election of German Kings and their claims for the Imperial Title do not require papal approval.
1339 - Beginning of the Hundred Years' War
Edward III of England lays claim to the French Throne, which Philip had inherited. This starts a war which will last over a hundred years.
May 7th, 1342 - Clement VI becomes new Pope
After the death of Pope Benedict XII, Clement VI becomes the new Pope and renews the excommunication of Louis the Bavarian.
July 11th, 1346 - Charles IV elected king
After all sorts of political intrigues, Count Charles IV of Mahren is elected Anti-King in 1346 in preference to the unpopular Louis the Bavarian.
October 11th, 1347 - Louis the Bavarian dies
King Louis IV, called the Bavarian, dies in the monastery Fürstenfeldbruck. Charles IV is generally recognized as King of Germany.
April 7th, 1348 - Founding of the first University in Prague
On 7 April 1348, Charles IV founds the first university of the Holy Roman Empire in Prague. The first university ever founded by Princes was built in Naples in 1224.
March 3rd, 1349 - Pogroms of Jews in German Towns
The Jews are made responsible for the Plague. One of the reasons for this is the fact that numerous noble and bourgeois people owe money to the Jews.
Dezember 18th, 1352 - Innocent VI becomes  Pope
Innocent VI is elected successor to the deceased Pope Clement VI in Avignon. The good relations between the Pope and King Charles are maintained.
April 5th, 1355 - Charles IV is elected Emperor
On his journey through Italy, King Charles IV has himself appointed Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire by a papal nuncio.
January 10th, 1356 - Golden Bulle forbids the alliance of towns
On the Reichstag in Nuremberg, King Karl IV declares the "Goldene Bulle. One regulation among others prohibits the alliance of towns.
October 14th, 1360 - Peace between England and France
France and England make a peace-contract in Calais. Edward III renounces the French Crown. In return, territories in France are granted to him.
January 16th, 1362 - Storm-tide on the North sea
De grote Mandränke, an enormous storm tide rages at the coast of North Friesland. The mainland is torn apart into separate islands.
November 1367 - The Pope returns to Rome
In 1367, under pressure from Charles IV, Pope Urban V relocates the residence of the Church from Avignon to Rome.
1368 - Charles IV on second Italian journey
King Charles IV starts his second journey to Italy, thus supporting the return of Pope Urban V to Rome.
March 28th, 1369 - New outbreak of war
The Hundred Years' War between England and France breaks out once again.
September 24th, 1370 - Unrest drives the Pope out of Rome
Pope Urban V flies from Rome due to unrest and returns to Avignon. He dies there a short time later.
June 5th, 1372 - Naval battle at La Rochelle
A fleet of Castilians, being allied with France, severely defeat England in the naval battle at La Rochelle.
October 20th, 1375 - Charles IV visits Lubeck
Charles IV, Emperor of the Holy Roman Empire, visits Lubeck and recognizes the importance of the town by nobly addressing the Patricians with: "Gentlemen".
January 1377 - Pope returns to Rome
Under Pope Gregory XI, the Head of the Catholic Church finally returns to Rome, after having resided in Avignon since 1309.
April 9th, 1378 - Papal election in Rome
Pressured by the people, Urban VI, an Italian, is elected Pope, succeeding the deceased Gregory XI.
September 17th, 1384 - Butchers uprising
The uprising of butcher's in Lubeck is quashed. Like many other trade guilds, the butchers reject the reign of the Patricians in the town council.
1390 - First paper mill in Germany
The first sheets of paper in Germany are produced in Nuremberg. Spanish Moors brought this Chinese invention to Europe for the first time in 1150.
November 11th, 1417 - The Schism comes to an end
The competing Popes, John XXIII and Gregory XII, are pressured to abdicate and make way for the election of Pope Martin V. The Church's schism ends after 39 years.
May 7th, 1429 - Joan of Arc in Orleans
Orleans, which has been under siege by  English troops for months, is liberated by French soldiers led by the peasant girl Joan of Arc.
May 30th, 1431 - Joan of Arc to be burnt
In Rouen, Joanne of Arc is accused of heresy by the English and burnt. The war between France and England ages on.
1453 - Hundred Years' War ends
After the victory of King Charles VII of France over the English troops at Castillon, the war which had started in 1339 comes to an end.
August 1456 - The Gutenberg Bible is published
The first printed bible with over 1.200 pages and an edition of 180 pieces is published in Mainz. Gutenberg had invented the printing of books in 1445.
October 12th, 1492 - Discovery of America

Christopher Columbus reaches the island of San Salvador with three ships and officially takes possession of it for Spain. At first, he misguidedly thought that he had discovered the much sought after sea route to India.
October 31th, 1517 - 95 theses against the selling of indulgences
Martin Luther reads out 95 theses against the selling of indulgences at the castle church of Wittenberg. As a result, the division of the Churches develops in the course of the following years.
May 24th, 1543 - Nicolaus Copernicus dies

Nicolaus Copernicus, born in Thorn, publishes his works on the solar system only a short time before his death. In this work he presents the opinion that the sun, not the Earth, is the fixed center of the solar system.
1669 - Last Hanse Meeting in Lubeck
In 1669, the last official meeting of the Hanse takes place in Lubeck. Only 9 German Hansa towns participate, among them Bremen, Hamburg and Lubeck.ýýýý­º««««««««

My dear Son!

You are old enough to tread in my footsteps, but first of all you should gain your own experiences.

Before I, because of my political obligations, settled down in Lubeck and married your mother, I was a travelling hawker and captain of a proud snaikka, and at home throughout the whole area of the Hanse. I would like you to follow my footsteps and gain admission to Hanse through your own resources. As start-up capital you are getting nothing more than a snaikka, a trading office in Lubeck, so that we can get to see you from time to time, and some cash. It should be easy enough to make it to a trader with this.

Your loving father

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
Dangers

My dear Son!

You have indeed enjoyed an excellent education, and one in which you could count the cleverest brains in Europe as your tutors, but so far you have never left the mainland.
So let me give you some good advice on the way: Be careful of  "travelling hawkers" in the same way, as you should be of the ship's kobold! There are many dangers awaiting you on the wide-open oceans, but this ghost ship is a monstrous creation of the devil himself. 

God protect you!
P.S. Your mother worries about you, so do not be too boisterous in your youthful high spirits!

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
Illness

My dear Son!

I observe with joy how well your business is flourishing. If you continue in this way, then you will easily make it to trader and way above that.

However, think not only about your own personal financial profit, but also about the needs of the people with whom you trade in the towns! Do not forget; wealth causes loneliness!

There is also a sad reason for my writing to you, your mother is not well, she has been in bed with high fever for days now, and the best doctors in the Hanse are at a lost as to what sort of rare illness it might be. I am sending to Florence for a doctor; hopefully, he will arrive in time!

Loving greetings, from your mother as well. And take care of yourself.

Georg Jantzen
{%-:00}GJ
Joy and sorrow

My Dear Son!

Why must joy and sorrow always have to be so close together?  I had hardly said goodbye to the Lord Mayor, who told me about your imminent appointment to trader, when master Ardovini summoned me. In my last letter to you, I spoke about this famous doctor. He arrived in Lubeck two weeks ago, but not even he was able to treat your mother's puzzling illness. She died suddenly two days ago, after her condition had remained stable for a long time and the hope of her recovering had begun to grow. Her body will be put to rest in the crypt in Lubeck next Sunday. And I feel the ravages of time nibbling at me in an above average way.

In spite of this gloomy news, please accept my best wishes on your quick advancement!

Your loving father

Georg Jantzen

Dear Leopold!

It is now hardly a week ago since I last wrote to you.  I buried your mother yesterday. You are now the only one that I have left.

God have mercy on my sinful soul, and do not let me loose you as well! You are a prudent trader, and I am sure that you won't disappoint me. Enclosed with this letter I am sending you 50,000\C, to speed up your career.

As soon as you have made it to a long distance merchant, I will tell you a secret that has been a burden on my conscience for a long time.Do not ask me about it, I can't tell you about it yet. In any case, not before I am certain that... No!  Go away, I told you that, I wouldn't betray it...

\f1_Young Sir!

Mission objective

You now have a year to rise from shopkeeper to trader.

Luebeck's strengths lie in fishing and the production of iron goods. Wood and bricks are also produced there, so you shouldn't have any problems constructing new buildings.

On the other hand, Luebeck only produces a little grain and no beer at all. So first of all, you should concentrate on getting beer from Stettin or Gdansk. You can also go to Hamburg or Bremen, but they are both further away.

Gdansk is always short of iron goods and sometimes of fish too. Stettin also urgently needs iron goods.

Make sure that you don't pay too much for the goods. The limits are around 450\C for fish, 450\C for iron goods and 50\C for beer.

Because trade in iron goods is important, you should ensure that there is always enough pig iron in Luebeck, as this raw material cannot be produced here.
This is however produced in Oslo, for instance. This town is also an appreciative buyer of grain, iron goods and beer.

However, you should always sell as many goods to Luebeck as possible, as this is the quickest way to increase your recognition, so that your advancement to trader status will not take too long.

Incidentally, don't start producing any buildings or ships yet. We can come back to that once you have achieved trader status.

Now you must make it from trader to merchant status. You have 6 months to do this. Besides trading, you should now build facilities and town houses in your home town.

As you know, Luebeck's strengths are fishing and the manufacture of iron goods. Start by building a facility for each of these industries. You may have to get the raw building materials for these from other towns. But you should only construct one of each building to start with, as you will also have to find buyers for your goods.

Building facilities brings you two advantages besides trade: firstly, your reputation grows with every worker that you employ. Secondly, creating new workplaces draws new citizens into the town. This increases demand and you can sell more goods.

If your facilities are to fill up with workers quickly, the poor townspeople must at the very least be contented. You should therefore continue to take good care of the town. The workers also need somewhere to live. If existing town houses are too overcrowded, you should build a new one.

Bear in mind that your facilities need raw materials. These must be available from your trading office.

If you have a trading office manager, he can buy in the raw materials when the town needs them. You don't need to worry about this at the moment though, especially since a manager also costs money.

To see which raw materials your facilities need, click on a facility once it is completed. You can also find out from your trading office what all of your facilities in the town need.

To become a merchant, you naturally need to acquire even greater recognition and amass considerable wealth. You should concentrate on cloth, wine and meat for the richer inhabitants of your home town. Try adding furs too - you will find them in the east.

If you should ever happen to come across spices, buy them! They are another much sought-after product with the rich citizens of Luebeck.

To transport the manufactured goods out of the town more efficiently, you should own at least one more ship. Commission a snaikka or crayer from the Luebeck shipyard.

Use your Luebeck shipyard as often as possible - including for repairs - because the more orders it gets, the better the ships will be that are built there.

All you need to advance from merchant to long distance merchant is a bit more recognition and some extra wealth. You must also be a member of the guild - which is sure to increase your reputation.\nOnce again, you have 6 months to complete your rise in status.\n

Bear in mind that your wealth includes not only your cash, but also facilities, town houses, ships and stored goods. However, any debts that you have with the moneylender are deducted.

If living space becomes limited in Luebeck, you should quickly build an appropriate number of town houses, as every tenant will bring you - just like every worker that you employ - additional recognition amongst the tenants. If you are too slow, your competitors, or the town itself may build town houses, in which case you will find it harder to fill your own. As the town houses also cost you weekly land taxes, they must be adequately populated to ensure that you can make a profit. The utilisation rate for half-timbered houses must therefore be over 70{%%:00}, while the utilisation rate for other houses must be at least 50{%%:00}.

Have you joined the Luebeck Guild yet? You must be a member of a guild before you can attain the status of long distance merchant or higher.\nBy the way, the guild entry fee increases as you become wealthier. It also decreases as your reputation in the town grows.\n

You must acquire a considerable increase in reputation with all the town's inhabitants within a year, if you are to advance to councillor status. As you also need to be much wealthier, you should invest as much as possible in your hometown, as investments increase your wealth and enhance your reputation.
Double or treble your production in Luebeck and build town houses in plenty of time, so that the new workers and their families can become your tenants. 
As your production increases, you also need to build new ships, so that the goods being produced can be transported.

Here are a couple more hints that may help you to improve your reputation.
Basically, all you need to know is that everything you do for your home town means a better reputation. If you spend money on the church or the public bath, your reputation increases. If you issue a loan or construct buildings and facilities, it increases again. It can also benefit from family, organisation of a celebration, a large fortune or the provision of guard ships. 
But it can also deteriorate if, for example, a criminal offence comes to light, if you demolish facilities or if you demand a high interest rate when extending a loan.
Incidentally, your recognition can also increase following a successful expedition, as all Hansa towns benefit from this. Just undertake an expedition every now and again, and discover new places to sell your wares.

To enable you to gain even more profit from trade, you should build a trading office in as many other towns as possible and produce goods there. It isn't always cheaper to produce goods yourself than to buy them at a low price. But by producing goods yourself, you can be sure of a constant price and a consistent quantity. This is particularly useful for setting up trade routes, to ensure a continuous supply to your home town, for example, or to exchange your own goods between two or more trading offices.
But be careful how you select your facilities. Think about which goods the towns are still likely to need in the future. Because if you produce more than can be used, the goods will stock pile in the towns and the price (and therefore your profit) will decrease in the long run.

Tutorial
Operating the game interface
In this part of the tutorial, you will learn about the basic principles of using the game interface.
Ships
Ships are the basic capital of every travelling merchant. Travelling, as well as the hiring of sailors and captains will be explained. Ship building and repairing will also be described.
Trading

In this, the most important part of all, you will be told everything worth knowing about trading. This includes, purchasing, selling and the transportation of goods, as well as the system of offers, supply & demand, requirements and consumption. This knowledge will make you into a successful trader.
Building towns

A town is essentially divided into municipal buildings, houses and production facilities. As a simple trader, you can build houses to provide living quarters for new citizens. Building production facilities allows you not only bring those looking for work from the countryside into the town but also allows you to produce raw materials and goods.
Sea battles
In this last part of the tutorial, you will learn how to manoeuvre a ship during a sea battle as well as how to board enemy ships.
The advancement

This campaign is thought of as an introductory campaign. You begin as a small shopkeeper in Luebeck and have to advance to a Patrician in Luebeck within four years. During the campaign, you will receive hints and instructions, in the form of personal news, on how best to achieve your aims.
The flying trader

You are a young small shopkeeper from a rich Luebeck family. Your private tutor gave you a good comprehensive education, which even at that time anticipated the enlightening spirit of the renaissance. The world to which you are going is marked by deep religiousness and a sailor's superstitious belief in the ship's kobold. Will you make its as a competent trader in this world, as your father before you?
Campaign: Rise of the Hanseatic League

The Hanseatic League is in an appalling state. Corruption and pirates have been the ruin of many a town.
You have been away for many years voyaging south in search of new countries and business opportunities. On your return you find your business in tatters. The once prosperous town of Rostock, your hometown that you helped to thrive, seems to have been set back to almost the state you found it in.
Your friends on the council, however, have not forgotten you. Your hard work and honesty made you a well-respected and highly trusted council member. They therefore put their faith in you to rebuild the Hanseatic League. You will receive whatever support they can offer. Just don't expect too much.
Your first task is to get your operation in Rostock back up to speed. Once this is achieved, you can then turn your attentions to the other towns. You goal is to double the number of inhabitants in the Hanseatic League over the next 15 months.
Not an easy task, but achievable.
Mission: Reorganisation

How could this have happened? You have just returned from a cultural visit to the Mediterranean and severely regret your decision of entrusting your business to your cousin. In a few short months his sterling efforts have ensured that the business has almost reached a total state of collapse. Your accountants are wringing their hands, your workers and crews are scared for their jobs and the citizens fear an economic disaster.\nYou are going to have to roll your sleeves up and get stuck in. Over the next 3 months your fortune has got to be restored to exactly the same level as before you left. And that used to be a cool 3 million!
Mission: Poor Harvest

A late spring and relatively cool summer has caused a poor wheat harvest throughout the Hanseatic League area. Autumn already sees most of the wheat stocks depleted. The prospect of a severe famine threatens to empty the towns of its citizens.\nFortunately you have invested in fish and meat production facilities. Your task begins in November 1357. You have fisherman's huts in your hometown of Luebeck and cattle farms in Aalborg. You also have quite a bit of stock at your disposal. You should use your stocks of wheat and beer wisely, you will not be able to replenish them.\nYou will have succeeded in your task if the total population in the Hanseatic League area has not been reduced by more than 4000 inhabitants by the end of March, when wheat production restarts.
Mission: The Fire

You are a rich merchant in Luebeck. Your task starts a week before a large outbreak of fire there, which will see many of your buildings go up in flames. Your task is to rebuild the town after the fire. You have got 6 months to get the number of inhabitants up to the same level as before the fire.
Mission: The Black Death

The year of 1347 saw the beginnings of the great plague. This massive epidemic started in the Mediterranean and then gradually spread Northwest and later eastwards. Times of great economic uncertainty and disaster began in all countries bordering the Baltic and North Sea, with England being particularly badly affected. Sea trade was disrupted massively.\nYou start this mission as a travelling merchant in Gdansk in the year of 1349, shortly before the plague breaks out in London. You have about a month before the plague will start spreading through the German towns of Cologne, Hamburg, Bremen, Luebeck, Rostock and Gdansk. Your task is to supply these towns during the epidemic, and to help them prosper again once the plague has passed. Timely boosting of a town's healthcare provisions can influence the plague's duration and spread.\nThe original number of inhabitants in the Hanseatic League needs to be restored within 4 months of this mission's start to have successfully completed this mission.

\\f1_Welcome to Patrician 3, the maritime trading simulation set in the period of the Hanseatic League.\nIn this introduction, you will learn how to develop from a simple shopkeeper to a travelling merchant.\nYou can use the two buttons to the right of this text to move forwards and backwards between each step of this tutorial.

\f1_The tutorial is divided into several parts. In this part you will learn about the operation of the game console.

\f0_Instructions
\f1_You should choose an interface resolution of at least 1024 x 768 for this tutorial.

\\f1_Let us first look at the divisions of the game interface layout. It consists of five parts.\n\\f0_Main view\n\\f1_Towns and the nautical maps are shown here. At the beginning of a game you will always start in your home town, which, in this case, is Lubeck.
\\f1_The main view only shows a section of the town. Move the mouse pointer to the edge of the screen or use the arrows on the keyboard to change the view
\\f0_Mini-Map\n\\f1_Shows the whole area of the town. The rectangle indicates the displayed area. Change this display by using the mouse to move the rectangle.

\\f0_Title Bar\n\\f1_The title bar is placed at the top of the screen. If you are in a town, it will show the following, from left to right: population, the name of the town, the number of your buildings in the town, your money and the date.\nThere are also buttons hidden behind the small symbols on the title bar.

\\f0_Population Button\n\\f1_Click onto the population symbol in order to see the population distribution and the satisfaction of the citizens of this town. If arrows are visible behind satisfaction, then they indicate whether the citizens are becoming more, or less satisfied.
\\f0_Building Button\n\\f1_The building symbol changes the view of a building. You use it to differentiate between your own and other buildings.

\\f0_Money Button\n\\f1_If you click the money symbol, a window with the statistics menu will be opened. However, this menu will not be explained in this tutorial. To close a window, either click onto the close button at the bottom right hand corner of the window, or right click.

\\f0_Chronicle\n\\f1The chronicle is hidden behind the hourglass. The chronicle contains important public information. It is worth looking into it every so often, to keep yourself up-to-date about events in the Hanse. Close the chronicle by using either the close button or a right click.

\\f0_Selection or Election Window\n\\f1_Information about selected ships is displayed here. Now, let us test it.\nShift the cursor to the harbour of the town. You will see a ship by the name of "Viking". This is your ship. Click on it in order to select it.

\\f1_The selection window will now display information about the selected ship. You will see the ship's location under its name. If it is sent somewhere else, you will also see the destination here. The ship's load is next to it. The uppermost number shows the capacity; the number in the middle shows how much space goods have taken up. Finally, the number below shows how much space is required for crew and armament.
\\f1_Apart from that, the ship's speed in knots, the condition of the ship from 0 to 100%, and the crew are displayed here.\nNext to that is the armament strength of the ship.
\\f1_Under that, you will see a list of all the goods on board. Note that there are two units of measurement: load and barrels. One load equals exactly 10 barrels.
\\f0_Button Bar\n\\f1_Let's look at the button bar and go through them from left to right.\nThe first button displays the list of ships. Please click it.

\\f1_You can see which ships belong to you, what their names are, and where they are at the moment. You only have one ship in this tutorial; therefore the ship's list is displaying one ship only.\nThe ship list shows the name, type of ship, status and location, load and the value of the goods on board. You can switch between the display showing crew and armament by using the button below the list.

\\f1_Incidentally, there is a "go to" button to the left of each ship in the ship-list. If you click on this button, it will go to the spot where the ship is placed. This can be in another town or at sea. Try it out, in order to bring the ship "Viking" into your field of vision.\nThen close the ship list.

\\f1_The next button is the fast-forward. If you press it, the running time will be speeded up. Meanwhile, you can follow all your ships on the complete map. The fast-forward ends as soon as you press a mouse button, or one of your ships goes to anchor in a harbour.

\\f1_The news menu is hidden behind the next button. All the letters you have received are filed here. Click on this button and you will see the news menu, in which various news items have been filed. Click onto one of the topics and then onto news-item, in order to read it.\nClose the news, in the same way as with all other windows by using the close button or with a right click.

\\f1_You can use the last but one button on the news menu to configure the letters-file so that letters can automatically be deleted later on. You can also delete a letter by clicking it and then clicking the "delete" button on the right of the news menu.

\\f1_The next button on the button bar is the construction menu. You can use this menu to construct buildings in towns where you have a trading office. The trading office is simultaneously the home, office and warehouse of a trader.\nTrading office and building menu will be explained in the chapter after the next.

\\f1_If you click the town gate button, you leave the town and end up on the sea map.\nInstead of the town, the sea map will be displayed. You can as usual shift the clip by using the arrow keys on the keyboard.

\\f1_All towns, and your ships will be displayed on the sea map. Naval events and foreign ships are also visible here.\nYou can enter any town in which you have ships or buildings from this map. In this tutorial, you are only represented in Lubeck.

\\f1_Incidentally, the title bar has changed. As you are no longer in a town, four ship buttons are displayed. You can switch between ships using these buttons. However, there will be differences between anchored and sailing ships, and convoys.

\\f1_Apart from that the display will show how many ships are at anchor in a harbour or waiting for new orders.\nShips that are at the shipyard for repairs or expansion are not shown, because they cannot be given orders.

\\f1_To leave the map and get back to Lubeck, click the blue button near Lubeck on the map. The last button on the far right of the button bar takes you to the options-menu. You can load games and save them, as well as ending the game here.

\\f1_Yet another tip for operating with the mouse:\nYou can select objects such as ships and buildings by using the left click. By using a right click you can send the selected ship to another location. Apart from that, the right click is used to close a window in the main view.
\\f1_Tutorial 1 ends here. Click on the "continue" button to end this chapter and to start the next one. Or select "End game" in the options-menu, to get back to the main menu.

\\f1_Welcome to chapter two of the tutorial. In this part of the tutorial, we will have a closer look at the ships, including areas such as travelling and the signing up of captain and crew.\nNow click the forward button to continue.

\\f1_You are in the town of Lubeck. Move the displayed area to the harbour and select the ship "Viking" by left clicking on it. The ship will then appear in the lower right selection window.\nNow look at this window in detail.

\\f1_There is an anchor and the town name, Lubeck, underneath the name of the ship. The anchor and the location indicate that the ship is at anchor in Lubeck. Instead of an anchor there could be another symbol, for example, when the ship is at sea, but we will come to that later.

\\f1_In the line below, the display will first of all show the speed of the ship in knots. Of course, in the habour the speed shown is 0. Next to that you will see the condition of the ship, which, at the moment is 100%, the ship is therefore in tip-top condition.

\\f1_To the right you see the crew and armament of the ship. The figure indicates the number of sailors on board. The star means that there is a captain on board.\nThere are large and small balls displayed under the weapons symbol. Only a maximum of five balls can be displayed here, five small balls are equal to one large ball.

\\f1_The large barrel shows the ship's load. As already mentioned, the uppermost figure to the right of the barrel shows the ship's capacity. How much space goods have taken up is indicated underneath. The lowest figure shows how much space isrequired for the crew and the weapons. As there are no goods on board now, the mid-figure is at 0.
\\f1_Later on, the list of goods will be displayed in the blank space below these instructions.

\\f1_Let's now move on to the other buttons in the ship's menu. First of all, there is the crew information. Click the "crew" button. This once again shows the number of sailors and the amount of their daily pay. As the ship is at anchor, you can dismiss sailors and captain. However, you shouldn't do that now.

\\f1_Below the captain you can see three values: Trading bonus, travel bonus and naval battle bonus. A captain has the following standing. The older he is, the more experienced he is.\nThe other buttons in the ship's menu are not too interesting during the first few hours of the game and are explained in the handbook.

\\f1_We will now send the ship to another town. To do that, you have to select a ship. Now click the button, "leave town" on the button bar above the ship's menu.\nThis will display the large sea map.

\\f1_As advised, if the ship is still selected, the town in which the ship is placed will be shown centrally. As the ship is at anchor in the port, you cannot see it directly on this map. However, you can see a small banner with a ship and a number next to the town of Lubeck. This is the number of ships that you have in the town.

\\f1_Now click on this banner to display the ships in more detail. As you can see, the known ship list is opened. It shows all ships being at anchor in the town. Now click the "Lydia" in the list and note how the selection window displays it.

\\f1_By clicking on the arrow on the left next to the ship's name you select the ship and centre it on the monitor while the ship list is being closed. Alternatively, you could also double click on the ship's name. Practice this a few times and re-open the ship list by clicking the banner next to the town of Lubeck.

\\f1_Now select the ship "Viking" again and close the ship's list. The ship will be displayed in the middle of the screen. Now, drag the sea map to the right and upwards until the town of Riga is displayed. Now do a right click on the red button near Riga, in order to give the ship the destination of Riga.

\\f1_The selection window now shows the changed status of the ship. Instead of an anchor symbol, you will now see a ship, and Riga as the town of destination. The estimated time of the journey in days is also shown.
\\f1_You may have noticed, that it took a while before the ship became visible at sea. The reason for this is that the ship spends some time in the harbour before appearing on the sea map.

\\f1_Incidentally, as soon as the ship is on the sea map, you will also see it on the mini map. Your ships have blue squares; selected ones have flashing squares. Sometimes also white squares are visible. These are ships of your competitors being within visible range of one of your ships.

\\f1_Now that the ship is on the way, we have got a bit more time to have a closer look at the sea map. Move the map in such a way that Lubeck becomes visible again. While all other towns have a red button, Lubeck has a blue one; showing that Lubeck is your hometown.

\\f1_As soon as you have set up a trading office in another town a blue spot appears on the red button. In this way, you can easily see in which towns you have trading offices.\nAll your property and towns are always indicated in blue.

\\f1_And remember: You can always recognise which towns you have ships at anchor by the banner next to the town. Click once more on the banner next to Lubeck. As there is only one ship in the town, it will be selected at once. It is the Lydia. Now do a right click on any point you wish in the middle of the ocean.

\\f1_With this right click you have instructed the ship to carry out an action, in this case, sailing to a position on the sea map. After a while, the ship becomes visible on the sea map.\nClick the left mouse button on an empty space in the ocean. This cancels all previous selections.

\\f1_Now wait until "Viking" arrives in Riga.\nAs soon as it arrives, the banner next to the town becomes visible. Left click  the red button, in order to enter the town. Note: you can only enter towns where you have a trading office or a ship at anchor.
\\f1_Now look at the mini map. It displays all buildings and streets of the town; the harbour and your ship are also visible. There is a button with an arrow on the left next to the map, click on it.

\\f1_You can use this button to switch between the sea map or the town map, but only when you are in a town. The nice thing about it, is that you can send your ship to another town without having to leave the town you are in.

\\f1_The towns are shown on the mini map by small diamonds. Look at the town at the very top of the map. This is Bergen. Now look for your ship in the harbour of Riga, select it, and right click on Bergen. As confirmation, the town flashes up for a moment, if it doesn't, then you have missed it and you should try again.

\\f1_Through the right click you have given your ship a new destination. The ship will sail to this destination and wait for further instructions.\nSo that we do not have to wait for too long for the ship to reach its destination, let's look at the fast forward.

\\f1_Click the "forward" button on the button bar using a left click. You will see at a total map of the whole see area, as well as all the ships that are on their way. Apart from that the time runs very quickly. The map remains displayed until a ship has reached its destination or you press a mouse button.

\\f1_Press the button whenever you are waiting for a ship to go to anchor. You will notice later on that there are other situations where the fast-forward ends automatically.\nWe will now wait until the "Viking" arrives in Bergen.

\\f1_Now enter Bergen by left clicking on it. Is your ship "Viking" still selected? If not, search for it in the harbour of Bergen and select it. As you can see, the journey has left its mark: the condition of the ship is no longer 100%. Therefore we have to repair it.

\\f1_Click the shipyard in the harbour of the town to enter it. At the shipyard, you can repair your ships, place orders for new ships,increase the ship's armourments or change the name of a ship. We are only interested in the button "repair ship". Please click on it.

\\f1_Using the book, you can switch between all ships at anchor and those in need of repair. Under the book you can see the cost of repair and underneath that, the button to place the order for repairs. Click this button and then leave the shipyard.

\\f1_When you have selected the ship, the selection window will show you how long the estimated repair will take. Of course, this depends on the current ship's status. Now wait until the repair is completed. You can also use the fast-forward button for that.

\\f1_Perhaps you are wondering where to hire crew members for your ship. This takes place in the taverns. Search the centre of Bergen for a tavern. A tip: they have wine barrels on their walls and they are near the shipyard. Do a left click on the tavern.
\\f1_There are certain people in the tavern with whom you can talk. They are not always there, but sailors looking for work are almost always there. Click the sailor's button.
\\f1_As a practice exercise, take on 5 sailors by transferring sailors from the tavern to ship, and clicking the button, "hire sailors".

\\f1_In a similar way, you can employ captains - in so far as they are present. Remember that each ship can only have one captain, and consider that unemployed captains are very much sought after, and are rare in any case.

\\f1_There are other people in the tavern are e.g, the informer, the pirate captain and the weapons dealer. Also you can meet travellers and other interesting people who have been in contact with you by letter.

\\f1_Now let us look at the construction of a new ship. Go back to Lubeck as it is advantageous to place an order for a new ship in the shipyard of your hometown. Change over the sea map and then click on Lubeck to enter the town. Then select the shipyard.

\\f1_Select the "Building contract" button in the shipyard. Now use the book to choose a ship. In the beginning of a new game, there are three ships to choose from. If the shipyard gets orders on a regular basis, its quality improves and it can offer better ships. Select a ship and follow the instructions for construction.

\\f1_Below the book to the right, you can find the construction time and building costs, and underneath the raw material requirements. Building a new ship requires a lot of raw materials. You have to have them either in stock at your trading office or you have to buy them directly from the town, if available. The estimated construction time is given in days.

\\f1_In this tutorial, the necessary raw materials are in stock at your trading office, so you do not have to buy them elsewhere. Now confirm the construction of a ship. However, because building a new ship takes a very long time, we will not wait for its completion in this tutorial.

\\f1_Always think very carefully before you place an order to build a new ship; the procurement and maintenance costs are very high. Also bear in mind, that only Snaikka and Crayer can sail to the river towns of: Cologne, Torun and Novgorod. The bigger class of ships cannot navigate the rivers.
\\f1_Here the chapter on ships ends. You can have a look around the tavern and dock if you like, before pressing the "continue" button to start the next tutorial.

\\f1_Welcome to chapter three of the tutorial, the most important part of the introductory course for would be maritime traders. It is about trading and everything connected to it, practical tips and valuable background information.

\\f1_We are going to look at purchasing, sales and the transportation of goods. Besides that, I will tell you how prices are created, how to recognise a good price, what requirement the citizens have and where best to buy or sell particular goods.

\\f1_But first of all, a few fundamental words about trading.\nCommerce is based on the fact that the towns produce different kinds of goods. On the other hand, however, the citizens and production facilities in the towns have a requirement for all goods. Therefore, each town has to import certain goods in order to flourish.
\\f1_It is you as a trader who supplies the towns with the required goods. Your competitors do the same throughout the Hanse area. You achieve three things in supplying a town:

\\f1_Firstly, citizens and facilities receive the goods and raw materials they require. This leads to higher satisfaction among the citizens, jobs are secure and new jobs can be created. Besides that, a good supply of goods and availability of work lure new citizens to the town.
\\f1_Secondly, the citizens notice when you make an effort to supply your town. Every item sold increases the respect in which you are held.

\\f1_Indeed, it must be your objective to attain the rank of a Patrician, and perhaps even to become Lord Mayor. If you succeed you can become famous beyond the borders of your hometown, you could even be elected as Alderman, the chairman of the Hanse.

\\f1_Thirdly, by trading with the right goods you could make really large profits. You could buy goods cheaply in one town where there is surplus to demand, and sell them at a higher price in another town where the demand is higher.
\\f1_You can use the profits to expand your business, for example, by building new ships or producing goods yourself.\nHowever, lets get back to the more practical side of things.

\\f1_We are back in Lubeck. "Viking" is at anchor in the harbour and you should now select it. There are a number of dock cranes on the quay. Left click on any crane you like to open the trading window.

\\f1_Dock cranes such as these are in every town. Using the trading window you can trade between town and ship, between town and trading office, as well as between ship and trading office. You can choose the direction of trade by using the buttons in the selection window.
\\f1_The menu will only appear if you have a trading office in the town, and a ship has been selected, only then you do have a choice of trading possibilities.

\\f1_Now choose trading between town and ship. On the left, you see the goods that the town has available, and on the right, the goods which are on the ship. As we have just started, there aren't any.
\\f1_The buy and sell buttons are between town and ship. There is already a price on each button. Buy means, you buy. Sell means, you sell.

\\f1_As you can see, the town pays less for a product than the purchase price you had to pay. This is, so to speak, the profit margin of the town. If you buy a product and resell it immediately, you make a loss. You have to sell the product where it is expensive.
\\f1_Now buy as much fish as your ship can carry. In order to do this, click on the relevant "buy" button several times. Your ship has a capacity for 15 loads of fish.

\\f1_Have you noticed how the price of the goods has increased during purchasing? This is because during your purchase the supply in the city has decreased. Note: The smaller the supply, the higher the price. The price falls correspondingly on selling the goods.

\\f1_However, the price depends, not only on the supply but also on the demand of citizens and business in the town, as they have to live from the goods that are available in the town. Note: the greater the demand, the higher the price.

\\f1_There is a figure next to the fish you have just bought. This is the average price that you have paid per product unit. You now have to find a town which will pay you more than this price. Only then can you make a profit.

\\f1_Incidentally, not all goods are measured in loads. Rare goods are measured in barrels; one load takes up the space of 10 barrels. Next to the ship's name you can see that the 15 loads of fish take up the whole cargo space, which is 150 barrels.

\\f1_As fish is produced in Lubeck, a large amount at a reasonable price is available. Now let's have a look at what other kinds of goods are produced in Lubeck. Now close the trading window with a right mouse click.
\\f1_There is a building standing on columns not far from the harbour. The indoor market is behind the columns. Click this building, it hides a lot of very interesting information.

\\f1_Here you can also see what other goods are produced in the town. Click the "production" button. As traders have not yet opened a business in this town, only the production of the town's own facilities will be on display.

\\f1_With the "consumption" button you can have the display show you which goods and how much the citizens and businesses consume each week in the town. With these information you can estimate how long the goods will be available.

\\f1_Now let's travel to a town that does not produce fish. London is such a town. Close the market hall, select your ship and indicate London as its destination. With a little help from the fast-forward option, you'll be there in no time.

\\f1_Now go to the sea map and click on London to enter the town. Click the dock crane, but remember your ship has to be selected. Sell as much fish as you can until the price people pay you, drops below the average price that you yourself paid.

\\f1_If you did not manage to sell all your goods, you can try some other towns. But before you leave, you should try and buy some goods at a reasonable price. However, how does one recognise if an item is on offer at a good price?
\\f1_Initially, you should have a look in the market hall to see how high the consumption and stock of particular goods is. The longer a product lasts, the lower the price will be.
\\f1_There is also some information in the trading window; observe the difference between purchase and selling price. The bigger the difference, the bigger is the demand of the town.

\\f1_A difference in price of about 10% is acceptable, however, you should never buy goods that are nearly twice as expensive to buy as to sell. Such a product is in short supply in the town; you would therefore have difficulty in selling it at a profit.

\\f1_Now look at the buttons below in the trading window. Here you can indicate the number of items which you wish to trade. Whether you buy 5 products at once, or make 5 single purchases of one product really doesn't matter as the total price is same in either case.

\\f1_Itemisation merely serves to help you to trading in large quantities. The "max" button takes into consideration how much cargo space is still available for goods you are going to purchase. On selling it considers, how many goods on the ship are available. In that way you can sell everything in one go.
\\f1_The basic principles of trading have now been explained. The best way of learning is for you to start on your own.

\\f1_Before ending this chapter, I would like to give you some information on the structure of the population in a town. You have already learnt that there are poor, wealthy and rich people in a town. Each group has its own particular needs.

\\f1_While poor people need basic foodstuffs such as wheat, fish and beer, the rich have more expensive needs such as meat, wine and cloth at the top of their list. The wealthy are somewhere between the rich and the poor.

\\f1_An increase in your social or economic standing depends on which group you primarily provide with goods.\nYour popularity does not only increase with the selling of goods. Everything you do for the benefit of the Hanse and its citizens, takes you further to the top.
\\f1_Click the "continue" button to end this chapter.

\\f1_In the fourth chapter of this tutorial, we will deal with the building up of towns and their growth. You will learn what buildings are important for the creation of towns, and what buildings you can build yourself to speed up the building of a town.

\\f1_Each town consist of action houses, dwellings and production facilities. Action houses are buildings where you can do certain things. You already know the dock and the tavern. Other buildings are the church and the municipal building. A Hanse town like Lubeck has 12 action buildings.

\\f1_In the first instance, your most important building is your trading office. In Lubeck, it is placed on the left near the seafront. In your hometown, the trading office is also  your living quarters, office and warehouse. In other towns it presents a branch of your trading company.

\\f1_However, within the framework of the tutorial, we won't be speaking about every single building in detail.\nBut note that you can click on any building in Patrician 3, and that the action houses are always in the harbour area or near the market square.

\\f1_Apart from the auction houses, there are also dwellings and production facilities. The production facilities produce raw materials and goods, the workers and tradesmen as well as their families live in the dwellings.
\\f1_You can build production facilities and houses wherever you have built a trading office.
\\f1_Another advantage of a trading office is that you can enter the town even if you do not have a ship at anchor in the harbour.\nAs already mentioned, such towns are marked in blue on the sea map.

\\f1_Now let's look at the production facilities in Lubeck. Since each town has other geographical prerequisites and also historically the skills of the population varied in the different towns, you can only build certain facilities in each town.

\\f1_Now open the building menu. It is the fourth button on the button bar. The building menu contains the trading office building, municipal buildings, raw material and production facilities, as well as fortification measures. Click once on each category to see what is hidden behind it.
\\f1_You cannot select fortification because you only have access to fortification after you have become Lord Mayor of a town.\nNow select "finishing companies" and then "workshop".

\\f1_In the selection window you will now see the building costs, construction time and the  building materials required. These materials will be taken from your trading office if they are available there. If this is not the case, then they will be bought directly from the town.The purchase prices applicable are displayed.

\\f1_It may occur that a particular building material is neither available in the town nor present in your trading office. In this case, you will have to buy the required raw material from another town before you can construct a building.

\\f1_ For the workshop, however, this is not the case. Since enough raw materials are available, you will see all the building plots that the town's planning office has allocated to you marked on the town view of the mini map.

\\f1_Now move the mouse over one of these building plots. You can also use the arrows on the keyboard to get a visible plot. If you move the mouse pointer over a building plot, the workshop lights up. Please left click.

\\f1_A building site appears and raw materials as well as money are deducted. Now choose "back" in the selection window to exit building. If you look at the building site for a while, you will see how the building slowly takes shape.

\\f1_Now activate fast-forward for as long as it takes to complete the workshop. Now click the finished building. At first, you will be shown how many workshops you own in Lubeck. Next to the workers symbol, you can see how many workers are currently available and the maximum number required.
\\f1_All facilities of the same kind are combined at this stage. Here, you can also decide the capacity of the facilities.

\\f1_Below, you will see what kind of raw materials the facility needs and what goods it produces. Iron ore and wood is needed in the case of the workshop, where iron-goods are produced. In order for this facility to start producing, you will have to have the raw materials available in your trading office, which is currently the case.

\\f1_Now look at the total cost: it is the weekly overheads of all companies of this kind. It is made up of basic tax, maintenance and wages costs. To keep production costs low, that is, the production price per goods, you must try to keep the facility running at full capacity.

\\f1_Note that the production cost of a given item is not the same in every town. In some towns goods can be produced on especially favourable terms, in others less so, and in others no goods at all can be produced. Production costs are correspondingly higher in towns with low production. Please have a look at the enclosed map.

\\f1_Incidentally, you can get information about facilities that you did not build yourself. The mini map show buildings belonging to you and those belonging to someone else. Your buildings are coloured blue, those of others traders are white, and those of the town are grey.

\\f1_You can also click the house symbol in the title bar. This will show the facilities and houses which were built by others. This is very useful because it shows the presence of your competitors in the town and your own presence in comparison.

\\f1_Now let us build a living house. For this you need to know that per worker in the town, four citizens on average have to be accommodated in a house as every worker also has a family. If there is not enough accommodation available, the number of workers cannot increase.

\\f1_You can find out how high the percentage of occupancy is of the present housing by clicking on a house.\nEach living house consists of three stages, of which you can only build the first. The later stages are reached as more and more people move into it.
\\f1_If all living houses have reached the third stage, it is a sign that accommodation is becoming short in the town.\nNow build a half-timbered house for the poor people in town.

\\f1_Now proceed with this building as you did with the workshop. After it is completed, you can watch the people moving in. In order for it to become full, there has to be work available in the town. Then beggars can become workers and advance to the poor citizens class.

\\f1_To do so however, the quality of life of the poor has to have a certain standard. If the poor citizens of the town are dissatisfied, because, for example, there are not enough goods available, beggars will not come into town and consequently you cannot employ any new workers.

\\f1_The population of a town consists of: beggars, poor, wealthy and rich people. Each group has its own requirements and consumes certain goods. Wheat, for example, is very important to the poor, whereas wine and meat is more important to the rich.

\\f1_Now click once on the population symbol on the title bar. In one window you will see the size of each group on the display. Note, that there are always fewer rich than wealthy, and fewer wealthy than poor people in a town.

\\f1_In this window, you can also see how satisfied a particular group is. A dissatisfied or angry group of citizens cannot grow; on the contrary, it will shrink. To satisfy the citizens of a town, at the least, the most important goods must be available.

\\f1_Incidentally, once a group has become mutinous, it'll take some time to get the mood back to normal again, therefore, you have to have patience. On the arrow to the right of "Satisfaction" you can recognise whether the mood of a group is improving or getting worse.
\\f1_But luckily, you are not the only trader who transports and supplies goods. However, you can have great influence on whether a town really grows to become one of importance.

\\f1_Apart from the availability of goods however, there are other factors that influence satisfaction. Wells, hospitals, good roads and the defence situation can all to some degree improve the quality of life in the town.
\\f1_Now click the "continue" button to end this chapter.

\\f1_Welcome to the tutorial on sea battles.\nDuring your long journeys through the sea area of the Hanse, you can repeatedly be attacked by pirates who, unfortunately, have nothing else in mind than to steal your ship and its cargo.

\\f1_If you meet a pirate on the sea map, you will be informed about it and additionally asked whether you want to handle the sea-battle automatically or manually. If you select manually, you will see this sea-battle view.

\\f1_As only three empty ships are involved, you have nothing to fear from your enemy on this occasion. But you can practice how to navigate a ship during a sea battle. First of all, select your ship "Viking" and look at its data.

\\f1_As you can see the deck is displayed automatically. The ship is a crayer that has twice had additional armour added in the shipyard. As a result of this it has lost cargo space, but at the same time, has increased its armament ability, as you can see from the 8 small catapults.

\\f1_By the way, a ship also gains more stability by adding armour.\nNow let us observe the functions and displays of the deck. At first, speed, condition, crew and weapons strength are shown. Next to that is the button "Fire"

\\f1_Your ship automatically shoots in the enemy's direction with "fire". Click on this button now. You will then see how a salvo leaves your ship and lands in the water. Apart from that, you will notice that it takes a while for the ship's weapons to be reloaded.

\\f1_Instead of clicking "fire", you can also press the space bar on the keyboard or the number 0 on the numbers block.\nUsing the "Capture" or "Plunder" button you are giving you ship the signal to board the enemy if possible, trying to capture or plunder the enemy vessel.

\\f1_Boarding will start as soon as the ships are close to each other and of course, you can only board a ship when your crew is superior in number.\nPlease note, that the ship deck functions are only at your disposal during a sea battle.

\\f1_Now let us get your ship moving. First of all, you have to set the sails. You do this by clicking the rope. You can change the height of the sails by using the keys, "page up" and "page down" on the keyboard.

\\f1_You can change the direction of the ship by right clicking on a spot in the water. You can also press the right mouse key, hold it, and move the mouse at the same time. The arrow on the water will then show you which direction the ship is now sailing in.

\\f1_Have you seen the clouds passing by? They are showing you wind direction and wind force. Always avoid sailing directly against the wind.\nNow set a course towards one of the ships. If the button "Capture" has been activated, please deactivate it.

\\f1_As soon as an enemy ship appears at the side of your ship, you should fire a broadside. Now cross backwards and forwards around the ship and try to sink it by firing broadsides at it. Try to take advantage of the momentum on manoeuvring, and avoid sailing against the wind.

\\f1_Now let us attack the enemy in another way. If you have selected your ship, simply right click onto an enemy. Your ship will now automatically attack and sink him. Make sure that "capture" is not activated; otherwise your crew will board the enemy ship.

\\f1_This automatic control is very practical when you are in battle with several ships.\nBefore moving on to the third ship, you should practice.As soon as the last ship has been defeated, the sea battle is over and the view changes back to the sea map.

\\f1_We are now going to board the third ship. Activate "capture" and right click on the enemy or approach him manually. The boarding fight will begin as soon as the ships are close enough to each other. As the enemy does not have a crew the situation is very quickly decided.
\\f1_After each sea battle, a summary is shown and you return to the sea map.
\\f1_We have now come to the end of the tutorial. Select "End Game" (Quit) in the options menu in order to return to the main menu.
